hold_text: `.github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml` is entry #1 in check_pr_landing.py's LANDING_MACHINERY, so R12 refuses to let this diff self-land by construction, and that refusal is correct: a change to the mechanism that opens and arms automation PRs must not be landed by that same mechanism. Needs a human merge click. What a human should check, stated so the click is not a rubber stamp: (1) the claim step passes --branch-claim and stages `.github/merge-slots` rather than docs/claude/session-board.json — those two lines ARE the change; (2) the new refusal fails the step when the script writes no claim, because an automation PR opened holding no R13 claim can never merge and would re-create the deadlock this action exists to end; (3) the session-board conflict-resolution branch further down is now UNREACHABLE from this action and is deliberately kept, with a comment saying why. NOT COVERED BY ANY TEST HERE AND THE REASON THIS IS THE RISKY PART: no automation PR has run through the changed action. 27 workflows call it, so if the claim step is wrong every automation PR fails to open — which is loud and immediate rather than silent, but it is fleet-wide. The tests execute the REAL extracted shell against a real git repo, which is the closest a harness gets and is not a workflow run.
why: Stops every automation PR writing the SHARED merge slot. MEASURED on origin/main 2026-09-12 over the last 40 commits: 18 touch session-board.json, ALL 18 change the merge_slot lines, and that includes ALL 3 automation commits — the mechanism BL-20260908-R13-MAKES-EVERY-AUTOMATION-PR-WRITE-THE-MERGE-SLOT-SO-MAIN-CAN-NEVER-BE-QUIET measured at seventeen consecutive conflict cycles on one PR. R13 accepts two routes and the legacy one still passes, so the per-branch route shipping with #11891 did not move the automation path; the route existing and the path taking it are different facts. Nothing is given up: R13 never serialized, so the shared field bought conflict and no exclusion, while attribution and timestamping are preserved and strengthened by the branch appearing in the claim's PATH as well as its body. One existing caller test pinned the shared route by name and failed a correct action; it now accepts either route, and staging NEITHER still fails — proven by planting it, not asserted. VERIFIED: 5/5 plants caught with the positive control quiet, 16/16 tests pass, and two concurrent automation claims reproduced against a real git repo running the REAL extracted shell, leaving session-board.json byte-identical. NOT claimed: no fleet observation, so the backlog row stays open rather than resolved.
